newsitem.title: USA: Nov chip industry book to bill ratio rises to 1.15.
newsitem.headline: Nov chip industry book to bill ratio rises to 1.15.

text.p: The semiconductor industry's key indicator rose last month, a trade group reported Monday, reflecting a 6.3 percent increase in orders for computer chips.

The Semiconductor Industry Association's book to bill ratio, which measures the value of orders against shipments rose to 1.15 in November from a revised 1.11 in October. The ratio means manufactures received $115 in new orders last month for every $100 in shipments.
Industry analysts had expected the ratio to be flat to slightly higher than October's level.

The ratio, a leading indicator of future demand tallied by the industry's trade group, has been improving recently, reflecting an increase in orders by personal computer makers and more stable prices for memory chip prices.
In a statement, the trade group said the November ratio is the highest since October of 1995 when it jumped to 1.16.
New orders rose 6.3 percent in November to $3.96 billion while shipments rose 2.9 percent to $3.44 billion.
The October ratio was revised from 1.10.

The ratio, which covers the Americas market, is due to be replaced next year by a global index. The Semiconductor Industry Association said the worldwide ratio for October, the latest period available, was 1.09.
Association officials said the increase in November marks the fourth consecutive month of real increases in orders and the third straight month of higher shipments.

"Given all that has happened in 1996, it's best to use caution in evaluating these numbers," said Doug Andrey, director of information systems for the Association. "But they are undeniably the best marks we've seen for the America's market all year. The third quarter doldrums are behind us."
While up from October, last month's orders were 19.4 percent below the year-ago period while shipments were 20.7 percent below November of 1995.
